content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to use a browser on a local network to enter a string and trigger the opening or closing of contacts on one of the outputs of a [product_name]? Regards
You can use the built-in web server of the [product_name] for this purpose.

Also, performing operations through the web server essentially hides how commands are being sent to the [product_name]. My question is: can I use a browser to access the IP address of the [product_name] and enter a string of characters to directly control its outputs?
Hello, I don't believe this is possible as described. However, you could use the web editor tool to create your own webpage with controls that interact with the outputs. Hope that helps.
Not every [product_name] device includes the extended web server feature.

The objective is to integrate customers who develop software in languages such as C++ or others, enabling them to use data from the controller to execute processes, and also to control the controller's outputs from their software.
If you're developing in C++, you could use the tool Snap7. This communication tool can interact with all [company_name] controllers, including those like [product_name]. Regards, [user_name]
In that case, it might be easier to use Modbus/TCP to access the device. It took me a while to understand, but now I routinely connect to [product_name] using LabVIEW or Python scripts.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are investigating options to control [product_name] outputs via a browser or custom-developed software. A frequent user challenge is the limited built-in support for executing direct commands or HTTP requests in these products. While some mention the native web server, they also note its restricted capabilities, and others suggest using third-party tools or protocols like Snap7 or Modbus/TCP for broader integration. There remains uncertainty about best practices for custom software interfacing, particularly for developers seeking solutions beyond the manufacturer's web interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to issue string-based commands through a browser or custom software directly to the [product_name] controller in order to control outputs and enable remote actions, and hope for a process that is straightforward and does not require complex integration.
